requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: A validated systemd unit named inventory-worker invokes the required executable, is enabled and active, and its live process is in the expected service cgroup. A bounded reboot changed the boot identity and the service recovered automatically in an active state with the executable checksum unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Run the service under a dedicated inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: The executor created a system account with its own UID/GID, locked credentials, a non-login shell, and no supplementary groups. Direct process and /proc observations before and after reboot show the service running entirely as UID/GID 992 for inventorysvc.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use service software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 are identical before and after execution and across the reboot. The existing systemd installation was used successfully without package changes, the worker checksum remained unchanged, and final package health was clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The required worker is an enabled, active inventory-worker service running under the dedicated inventorysvc account, and the original RHEL release, kernel, and worker were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the node became temporarily unreachable, a different boot ID was observed afterward, and service, executable, platform, SSH, and system health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Requirement req-1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-service-worker

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The account creation, unit-file creation and labeling, daemon reload, enable/start operations, and scheduled reboot were directly necessary for the requested service or mandatory restart evidence. The temporary login-test file was removed by the same command. Post-execution observations show no failed services, no new network exposure, healthy package state, and only expected reboot- and PrivateTmp-related temporary-directory turnover.
